label: Vintage early-1950s sports (1952 Topps class, 2-5/8 × 3-6/8 in)
size_source: PSA article (Joe Orlando): in 1952, the Topps cards measured 2-5/8" by 3-6/8" versus Bowman's 2-1/8" by 3-1/8" — https://www.psacard.com/articles/articleview/10365/new-era-begins-elements-make-1952-topps-baseball-card-set-most-iconic-postwar-age (2-5/8×3-6/8 in = 66.675×95.25 mm). Wider tol because of vintage cutting variance. Topps standardized 2.5×3.5 in 1957 (https://baseball.cards/guides/baseball-card-size-and-dimensions/).
back_cues: 1952 Topps baseball statistics / bio back; series-dependent
counterfeit_tells: trim to look like a smaller modern card
grader_notes: CGC maximum listed size is 2-5/8" × 3-3/4" (6.6 cm × 9.5 cm) — this class is at that cap. TAG accepts only 2.5×3.5 cards manufactured 1989–present, so TAG is not eligible. PSA app accepts tallboys and oversized holders; PSA chooses the holder.
